refuted.title: antipatterns.md is 815 bytes of generic best practice, loaded TWICE per session (verdict CUT)
refuted.reason: The file is NOT hand-written prose — it is a GENERATED ARTIFACT written by ork's own live hook on every SessionStart. src/hooks/src/lifecycle/sync-session-dispatcher.ts:32 imports materializeAntipatternRules and calls it at :79 (guarded only by isLightResume). src/hooks/src/prompt/antipattern-warning.ts:55-60 builds the exact 7 bullets from STATIC_ANTIPATTERNS and calls writeRulesFile(rulesDir,'antipatterns.md',...). The md5 identity the auditor cites as evidence of double-billing is actually evidence of a single generator: the sibling ~/.claude/rules/user-profile.md in the same system prompt is produced by materializeProfileRules() at profile-injector.ts:300-308 the same way. `git rm .claude/rules/antipatterns.md` yields a dirty tree that regenerates on the next session start. Byte saving from the stated action: ZERO. Second defect: the auditor asserts 'no hook reads them, no skill references them' logic elsewhere but never grepped here — 9 agent bodies cite the file by path as a mandatory step (backend-system-architect.md:77, ci-cd-engineer.md:68, event-driven-architect.md:77, test-generator.md:76, product-strategist.md:59, security-auditor.md:69, infrastructure-architect.md:68, code-quality-reviewer.md:72, frontend-ui-developer.md:81, all 'cross-check against .claude/rules/antipatterns.md'). Deleting the file breaks step 3 of nine agents. The correct action is to edit STATIC_ANTIPATTERNS in the hook (or gate materialization), and to fix the 9 agent references in the same commit — a source change, not a file deletion.

refuted.title: CLAUDE.md ships stale component counts two lines after telling you not to trust them
refuted.reason: The counts are CORRECT, and the auditor's counting method is the wrong one. They ran `ls -d src/skills/*/ | wc -l` = 115 and `ls src/agents/*.md | wc -l` = 37. But src/skills/shared/ has NO SKILL.md (it is the shared-rules dir), and src/agents/README.md is not an agent. The repo's own canonical counter, bin/validate-counts.sh:26-27, uses `find src/skills -name SKILL.md | wc -l` and `find src/agents -maxdepth 1 -name '*.md' | grep -viE '/(README|INDEX|CONTRIBUTING).md$' | wc -l`. Live: 114 SKILL.md files, 36 agent files — exactly what CLAUDE.md:27-28 says. 'Both wrong' is false; the whole evidence block for this finding is an artifact of a naive glob. (The orchestrator's briefing figure of 116 skills is also wrong for the same reason; validate-counts.sh:11 carries a stale 116 in a COMMENT, not in the assertion.) Deleting the counts may still be defensible on drift grounds, but the stated defect does not exist, and .claude/rules/count-sync.md:14 plus .claude/rules/agent-authoring.md:34 both mandate keeping them in sync — so this is a governance change requiring those two rules to be edited too, not a bug fix.

refuted.title: src/rules/code-quality.md and docstring-standards.md ... 'shipped into the plugin for 100% of ork users'
refuted.reason: They are not shipped. `find plugins -name code-quality.md -o -name docstring-standards.md -o -name license-compliance.md -o -name visual-style.md` returns NOTHING, and `grep -n rules scripts/build-plugins.sh` returns nothing — src/rules/ has no plugins/ mirror and the build never copies it. The auditor's own evidence sentence ('returns ZERO hits outside src/rules/ and the generated plugins/ mirror') describes a mirror that does not exist. Consequence for the cut: src/rules/*.md is also NOT in the .claude/rules auto-load path, so these files cost ZERO context tokens per session today. The orphan verdict on the content is fine; the 1,323 'bytes_saved' is disk bytes with no session-token effect, and the distribution-harm argument ('dead weight with a distribution channel') is fabricated.

refuted.reason: The auditor hedged but landed on 'fold the eval-schema line into test-conventions.md'. refuted.title: ci-workflows.md is 100% generic CI advice with no OrchestKit content
refuted.reason: Overstated. 3 of the 8 lines encode verifiable repo facts, not universal defaults: '.github/actions/' exists (contains run-tests/ and setup/); 'Pin action versions to SHA, not tags' is a policy the repo demonstrably enforces (every sampled `uses: actions/checkout@...` is a 40-char SHA with a trailing version comment, e.g. .github/workflows/build.yml:27), which is an OSSF-Scorecard-driven convention a fresh model will NOT reproduce by default when hand-writing a workflow; and 'never set -x in steps with secret access' is a real leak vector. '100% generic' and 'zero references to this repo' are both false. The 572 'bytes_saved' is also a per-session zero — the file carries `paths: .github/**` and only injects when a workflow file is touched.

CONTRIBUTING-SKILLS.md:621-627 is 318 bytes, not 600 (1.9x inflated), and that file is read-on-demand so the per-session saving is 0. Finding 18's headline bytes_saved 2,405 contradicts its own prose arithmetic in the same finding (815+260+45+420 = 1,540, giving 7,322 → 5,782). The user-global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md says 'Always respond in English unless explicitly asked otherwise.' The project file overrides a global escape hatch with 'No exceptions'. rules-meta.md:17 ('Rules compose: a file matching 3 rules gets all 3 injected') is exactly the failure mode, and the auditor filed CLAUDE.md:7 as generic 'noise' rather than as a live conflict.

No test asserts the CLAUDE.md skill/agent counts. `npm run test:manifests` (package.json:24) runs six scripts, none of which reads CLAUDE.md; the only CLAUDE.md assertion anywhere is tests/manifests/test-cc-version-floor.sh:68, which checks the CC floor string. That is the actual argument for deleting the counts (unenforced prose, drift-prone by construction) and it is stronger than the false 'they are already wrong' claim the auditor used.

Also note :104 wraps the check in `|| true`, so the shape of enforcement is softer than visual-style.md:83's 'Hard 4800-byte cap enforced by' implies — the auditor's proposed rewrite preserves the word 'Hard' while fixing only the path.

The recommendation to 'close the loop mechanically' was executed six days ago; the open question is now whether the ~180 static bytes in CLAUDE.md are still needed given the hook says the same thing.

Nothing enforces the cap: src/hooks/src/lifecycle/rules-size-check.ts exists (so the #1815 hook reference in CONTRIBUTING-SKILLS.md:212 is real) but it gates total chars, not per-file line count.

CONTRIBUTING-SKILLS.md:212 is quoted truncated. The full line continues 'The lifecycle/rules-size-check hook (#1815) warns at 35k chars so you have ~5k of runway before the cliff.' The auditor's proposed 'after' text silently drops that sentence, and finding 17 then recommends wiring up rules-size-check as if it were an unmade connection already documented on the very line being rewritten.
verdicts.notes:
Method: opened every cited file, re-derived every count and byte figure with wc/find/grep, and traced static wiring (hook entries map, agent frontmatter and bodies, build script, plugins/ output, package.json test scripts, git hooks) before accepting any 'dead' or 'generic' verdict.

Score: 11 of 18 findings survive intact, 4 are wrong at the evidence level, 3 are directionally right with fabricated or misattributed support.

The two failures that matter, both in the user's disfavour:

1. The report's single largest byte claim (antipatterns.md, 1,630) recommends deleting a file that ork's own SessionStart hook regenerates and that 9 agent bodies cite by path. Executing it produces a dirty tree, no token saving, and nine broken agent instructions. This is precisely the 'dead verdict that ignores static wiring' failure mode.

2. The 'stale counts' finding is an artifact of counting with `ls` instead of the repo's own bin/validate-counts.sh. CLAUDE.md's 114/36 are correct. Acting on it would have replaced accurate facts with a fabricated defect narrative.

Quote fidelity was otherwise high: cc-native-first.md, rules-meta.md, agent-authoring.md:20, usage-analytics-hardening.md (all four sections), CONTRIBUTING-SKILLS.md:529/:544/:623, visual-style.md:83, split-bundles.test.ts:343 and the shared/rules path collision are all verbatim and real. The corpus arithmetic (7,322 / 12,378 / 75,809) reconciles exactly. The best finding in the report is #6 (CONTRIBUTING-SKILLS.md:212 is false about how .claude/rules loads) — confirmed by direct inspection: exactly 2 of 12 .md files lack `paths:` frontmatter, and exactly those 2 appear in this session's system prompt.

On the operating thesis: the audit's own closing conclusion is the honest one and survives verification. The rule surface is 7.3KB/session against 121.7KB of always-loaded skill frontmatter. But the audit under-measures its own dimension by ignoring the per-turn hook systemMessage tax, which is the real ban-voice, zero-information surface in this repo and is not on anyone's byte ledger.

refuted.title: MCP probe ritual for a server the config already always-loads
refuted.reason: Two independent refutations. (1) The plugin ships NO .mcp.json: `find plugins -name '.mcp.json'` returns nothing, `grep -n mcp manifests/ork.json` returns nothing, and `ls plugins/ork/` is agents/CLAUDE.md/commands/hooks/mcp-server/settings.json/skills. The `alwaysLoad: true` entries the comment cites live in THIS REPO'S project-local /Users/yonatangross/coding/yonatangross/orchestkit/.mcp.json (lines 10, 18, 26). A plugin user in any other repo has no such guarantee, so the probe is live capability detection for the entire non-dogfood audience. assess's own frontmatter (:4) says `Requires memory MCP server` — the probe is how it degrades instead of hard-failing. (2) The auditor's 'a capabilities.json write nothing downstream reads unconditionally' is weasel-worded around a documented consumer protocol: src/skills/chain-patterns/references/tier-fallbacks.md:27 `caps = JSON.parse(Read(".claude/chain/capabilities.json"))`, :41 'Never assume MCP exists — always check capabilities.json'; also chain-patterns/rules/probe-before-use.md:27 and chain-patterns/references/mcp-detection.md:37, plus handoff-schema.md:9 which documents it as part of the chain contract. Nine skills write it and three references read it. Deleting the probe removes graceful degradation and breaks a cross-skill contract. The resume-check consolidation is fine; the probe deletion is not.

refuted.title: `ORCHESTKIT_FORCE_TASK_TOOL=1` is documented in 8 files and read by zero lines of code
refuted.reason: The load-bearing half of the 'why' is false. The auditor wrote 'no skill tells the model to read the env var, and the model cannot see env without shelling out — so even the honour-system version never fires.' Three files do exactly that: src/skills/assess/references/orchestration-mode.md:11 and src/skills/verify/references/orchestration-mode.md:11 both read `force_task_tool = os.environ.get("ORCHESTKIT_FORCE_TASK_TOOL") == "1"`, and src/skills/implement/references/orchestration-modes.md:8 is identical. Reading env is one `echo $VAR` away for a skill with Bash allowed. The narrow claim (`grep -rl` finds only .md, no hook/TS/settings) is true, but the flag is a user-set shell escape hatch on the honour system, which is a design choice, not a phantom. 'Under-tested' is the honest verdict; 'read by zero lines of code' as grounds for deletion is not supported.

refuted.title: Achievable reduction across the 15 used skills: ~95 KB of 255 KB (37%), zero information lost
refuted.reason: The 95 KB is not measured — it is roughly 2x the auditor's own arithmetic. Summing the `bytes_saved` field across every other finding in this same report gives 47,900 B (900+3100+11500+5300+600+12000+5000+2800+800+900+3500+200+1000+300). The headline claims 95,000. The per-skill target column is unbacked wherever no finding exists: `remember -5 KB` against a measured 8,786 B body with ZERO findings citing remember; `memory -2.7 KB` against 5,906 B with zero findings; `help -3 KB` against a 5,978 B body backed by exactly 900 B of evidence (a 50% cut on 15% evidence). Even the itemised line contradicts itself: 'brainstorm -17 KB (Agent Teams 6.5 + STEP 0a 2.7 + version quotes 2.5 + task block 1.4 + probe)' sums to ~13.5 KB, not 17. Verified body/frontmatter measurements are otherwise accurate (my measured totals: 231.1 KB body + 24.0 KB frontmatter = 255 KB, matching), so the base numbers are real and only the savings projection is invented. Defensible measured ceiling is ~46-48 KB (18-19%), not 95 KB (37%).

Comparison mode (design alternatives) adds Simplicity at 0.10 and rebalances — see references/quality-model.md; this rubric encodes the default mode.' So `simplicity` in the frontmatter description is a real mode, not a phantom. Only `scalability` and `compliance` are genuinely unadvertised. The rest of the finding is CONFIRMED and in fact stronger than stated: rubric.json carries exactly the 7 dimensions at :7-15 with `min_pass: 5.5`, and implement/SKILL.md:141 hard-gates Phase 1 on that file. Keep the finding, drop the 'three mutually exclusive sets' framing.

missed: THE BIG ONE — allowed-tools drift is ~10x wider than TaskGet, and the auditor's own KEEP recommendation walks into it. Cross-checking every tool call in each body against its `allowed-tools:` line at HEAD: commit/SKILL.md declares `allowed-tools: [Bash]` (line 13) and then calls AskUserQuestion (:71), Write (:177) and Read (:215, :253). The auditor's action item says 'Keep commit's mode question (:71) — amend-vs-new is irreversible', i.e. it recommends preserving a tool call the skill is not permitted to make. Also unpermitted: create-pr calls Write (:349) and Read (:149,:162,:207,:264,:375,:398) with neither declared; assess calls Write (:106); explore calls Write (:109); remember calls AskUserQuestion (:165); implement instructs EnterWorktree, ExitWorktree and WebFetch; brainstorm instructs ExitWorktree (inside the very block the auditor quoted, so their rewrite fixes it by accident without noticing). No test enforces the invariant, which is WHY all of the above shipped. tests/skills/audit-skill-permissions.sh only greps `^allowed-tools:` for presence (:56) and reports skills lacking the key (:105) — it never checks that the declared set covers the tools the body instructs. That gap is the root cause the report should have named; 'delete the TaskGet line from 8 files' fixes 1 of 11 tool names in 8 of 23 files and leaves the generator of the bug untouched.

The TaskGet line is in 23 SKILL.md files, not 8: audit-full:76, audit-skills:62, component-search:87, demo-producer:92, design-context-extract:107, design-to-code:134, expect:129, fix-issue:138, github-operations:63, notebooklm:81, release-management:58, setup:87, write-prd:94 all carry the byte-identical line on top of the 8 cited. A fix scoped to the live-skills dimension leaves 15 live copies that the next skill author will paste back.

create-pr's `dev` is in 6 places, not 4, and one of them is the expensive one. Missed: :24 `- "open a PR against dev"` sits inside the ALWAYS-LOADED frontmatter (the trigger list), so the wrong base branch is part of the per-session 30k-token index, not just the on-invoke body. Also missed :153 `[[ "$BRANCH" == "dev" || "$BRANCH" == "main" ]] && echo "Cannot PR from dev/main" && exit 1` — that one is correct as written (a defensive guard against both possible bases) and must NOT be swept up by a blind `dev`→`$BASE` substitution.

The help bug is already shipped, and no proposed action rebuilds. plugins/ork/skills/help/SKILL.md:59 carries the identical `path="src/skills"` Grep, so every marketplace install has it live right now. Per CLAUDE.md, plugins/ is generated and `npm run build` must be run and the diff staged; not one of the 18 `action` fields mentions rebuilding, so every edit as written would leave the installed plugin unchanged. Same applies to all the other cuts.

The report does not cut a single byte of the tax the user actually asked about. The dominant contributor is `description:` prose (assess's is 431 chars on one line; cover's is 621) plus per-skill `allowed-tools` arrays up to 240 chars. This is textbook INFORMATIVE by the brief's own definition — non-derivable, dated, incident-backed — and it was folded into the 3.5 KB 'AskUserQuestion ceremony' savings line without being called out as a keeper.

verdicts.notes:
Method: opened every cited file at HEAD, re-measured every byte figure with wc -c on the exact claimed line ranges, and cross-checked static wiring (rubric.json, .mcp.json, manifests/ork.json, plugins/, tests/skills/) rather than trusting quotes.

Citation accuracy: high. Every file:line I spot-checked exists and says what was claimed — assess:191/brainstorm:249/visualize-plan:78/verify:197/implement:261/explore:179/cover:173/create-pr:136 all carry the byte-identical TaskGet line; all 8 allowed-tools arrays verified to lack it; the 6 Progressive Output headers, 3 Focus mode notes, 4 /recap notes and 4 CronCreate blocks are all where claimed. Byte figures are measured, not invented: brainstorm 351-437 is exactly 6,514 B as stated; the eight task-ceremony ranges land within 0.3-8% of the claimed sizes; body/frontmatter totals reconcile to the claimed 255 KB. Only two small header miscounts: "Monitor + Partial Results (CC 2.1.98)" exists as a header in 2 files (verify:249, cover:431), not 3 — implement:319 has different text; and implement's Budget block is 1,003 B, not 1,098.

The four "live bugs" in the headline: three survive unchanged (TaskGet, cover's superseded worktree contradicting implement:340-345 and manual-worktree-pattern.md:3 verbatim, help's src/skills path which I confirmed is also live in the shipped plugin). The fourth (create-pr `dev`) survives but is understated — it also sits in always-loaded frontmatter at :24.

Where the report is dangerous: the MCP-probe cut would delete graceful degradation for every user outside this repo (the plugin ships no .mcp.json) and break a documented three-consumer chain contract. That is the one recommendation here that destroys real, repo-specific information. The 95 KB headline is 2x the report's own arithmetic and should not be quoted to anyone. Everything downstream of "the mechanical deletions (~31 KB)" is defensible; the aggregate is not.

Net: this is an unusually well-evidenced audit whose individual findings mostly hold, undermined by one wrong cut, one overstated dead-flag claim, and a fabricated total. Its largest omission is that the exact defect it leads with (TaskGet) is one instance of an 11-tool, 10-skill, untested class of frontmatter/body divergence — including one case where the report recommends preserving an unpermitted call.

H2 CONFIRMED: frontmatter wiring is the only non-derivable content (KEEP verdict is correct)
Agent Teams blocks name teammates that are not real registry names (backend-architect / test-engineer / code-reviewer)
Twenty agents carry stale CC-version and model-generation references that will keep rotting because nothing tests them
frontend-ui-developer's Browser Automation section (:129-214) is self-declared duplication of the browser-tools skill
Grounding Protocol self-refutation is real on 4 of the 6 named agents (frontend-ui-developer:78, ci-cd-engineer:66, product-strategist:56, test-generator:65-66)

refuted.title: H3 CONFIRMED: descriptions lack a trigger condition, and that is the direct mechanism behind 6,531 generic vs 1,135 specialist spawns (verdict REWRITE, bytes_saved 0)
refuted.reason:
The factual half is true (I confirmed only emulate-engineer:3 and genui-architect:3 carry a Use-when/Use-to clause; all 34 others are noun phrases, and the three quoted descriptions are verbatim). The CAUSAL claim and the ACTION are both refuted by the repo itself, which the auditor never opened.

(1) src/skills/audit-activation/rules/activation-status.md:38 - "**Never bucket on description quality.** A/B testing showed description rewrites give Delta-0 routing benefit - dormancy is a wiring problem, not a prose problem." src/skills/audit-activation/SKILL.md:92 - "**Never recommend rewriting agent descriptions.** A/B-tested: description rewrites gave Delta-0 routing benefit... the fix is always adding a subagent_type=ork:<name> spawn from a high-traffic skill... never prose changes." Same at SKILL.md:30, references/output-format.md:31, scripts/run-activation-audit.sh:119. The isolated A/B harness is checked in at docs/feat--activation-audit/agent-routing-experiment.mjs and scored 18/18 for BOTH the terse and the rewritten variant across 10 clear + 8 indirect prompts, including dormant agents on keyword-free phrasing. The auditor asserts the opposite as "the highest-leverage change in the whole dimension" without citing or refuting the in-repo experiment that already tested it.

(2) bytes_saved:0 and "it costs ~40 bytes per agent" are both false, and the action would hard-fail CI. tests/performance/test-token-overhead.sh:79-80 sets AGENT_DESC_SINGLE_MAX_BYTES=250 and AGENT_DESC_TOTAL_MAX_BYTES=6000. Measured at HEAD: 36 descriptions = 5,314 bytes total (686 bytes of headroom = 19 bytes/agent, not 40), max single = 249 bytes (1 byte under the cap). The auditor's own AFTER example for debug-investigator is 285 bytes - it violates the single-description cap by itself. Rolled to 36 agents at that length: ~10,296 bytes vs a 6,000-byte hard-fail cap, a 72% overrun. That file runs in package.json:21 `validate:pre-push`, so the proposal fails the pre-push gate. Descriptions are the ALWAYS-LOADED index - this finding makes the one genuine recurring token tax 94% worse while claiming zero cost.

refuted.title: 25 agents instruct the model to read paths that do not exist (verdict CUT, delete Context Protocol / Boundaries / Coordination / Execution from all agents)
refuted.reason:
The headline is false for the 25 Context Protocol references, which are the bulk of the finding. Verified at HEAD:
- .claude/context/session/state.json EXISTS and is live - it currently holds session_id 61366a40, last_activity 2026-07-26T22:13:58, and a populated `tasks_completed` array of real commit SHAs. That is exactly the field backend-system-architect.md:314 tells the agent to append to.
- .claude/context/knowledge/decisions/active.json EXISTS.
- A hook writes it: src/hooks/src/lifecycle/session-env-setup.ts:88-99 reads state.json, sets agent_type/session_id/last_activity and atomic-writes it back. Also referenced by src/hooks/src/setup/first-run-setup.ts:255, setup-maintenance.ts, setup-repair.ts, pre-compact-saver.ts, post-compact-recovery.ts.
- CI tests it: tests/run-all-tests.sh:173 ("Context Schema Validation") and :260 ("Context System Integration" -> tests/integration/test-context-system.sh, which validates the context://session/v1 schema).
So the Context Protocol is live, hook-maintained, schema-locked wiring - by the auditor's own definition, INFORMATIVE and non-derivable. Deleting it from 25 agents destroys real repo-specific information. This is the single worst call in the report.

The backend/app + frontend/src half is misreasoned rather than merely wrong. "Verified against the repo: backend/app MISSING, frontend/src MISSING" is the wrong test: ork is a plugin shipped INTO consumer projects (CLAUDE.md: "Claude Code plugin"; agents run against the user's tree, not this one). Of course an app layout is absent from a plugin repo. Those paths are a weak generic assumption, not a stale import from another project, and the auditor's stated proof does not establish what it claims.

Only the role-comm half survives: I confirmed `find . -name 'role-comm*'` returns nothing and exactly 2 agents reference it (frontend-ui-developer.md:487-488, code-quality-reviewer.md:226-227).

refuted.title: H1: 43% of all body text is copy-pasted boilerplate (4,094 / 9,452 lines across 18 templated sections)
refuted.reason:
The 43% number conflates "shares a heading name" with "is verbatim identical". I hashed every block:
  ## Task Management      34 blocks,  4 distinct, most common x31  <- genuinely templated
  ## Status Protocol      36 blocks,  3 distinct, most common x34  <- genuinely templated
  ## Output Format        33 blocks, 33 DISTINCT, most common x1   <- NOT copy-pasted
  ## Task Boundaries      35 blocks, 35 DISTINCT, most common x1   <- NOT copy-pasted
  ## Concrete Objectives  32 blocks, 32 DISTINCT, most common x1   <- NOT copy-pasted
  ## Resource Scaling     27 blocks, 27 DISTINCT, most common x1   <- NOT copy-pasted
Actually-verbatim content is Task Management (306 lines) + Status Protocol (246 lines) ~= 552 lines = 5.8% of the 9,452 body lines, not 43%. My own prefix-matched span measurement over 15 of the named sections totals 3,567 lines / 37.7% / 143,726 bytes - so the auditor's line arithmetic is in the right ballpark, but the word "verbatim" that justifies the CUT verdict is false for the four largest per-agent sections (Output Format alone is 1,073 lines, the biggest block in the dimension, and every one of its 33 instances is unique).

Also: '## Execution' and '## Coordination' appear in 2 files each, not "all 36" as the action implies. '## Opus 4.8: 128K Output Tokens' is 9 files, not 10.

The part that IS right: persona openers are exactly 10/36 and the file list matches mine byte-for-byte; the python-performance-engineer.md:150-219 cProfile/pstats/asyncio tutorial is real. But bytes_saved:160,000 is built on the false copy-paste premise, and this finding conflates on-spawn cost with always-loaded cost - agent bodies load ONLY on spawn, so cutting 160KB of body saves ZERO baseline session tokens.

refuted.title: CUT list: 12 agents whose entire job is a skill that already ships or a task Opus 5 does natively (6 never-spawned = dead)
refuted.reason:
Every one of the 36 agents is statically wired and the repo already has a gate that proves it. I ran tests/orphans/test-orphan-agents.sh: "Scanned: 36 agent(s)... All agents are referenced by at least one skill or hook." The auditor treated "never spawned in telemetry" as "dead" without running the orphan detector that exists for exactly this question.

The five "shadowing" agents do not shadow their skills - the skill DISPATCHES the agent:
- src/skills/design-import/SKILL.md:139 literally contains subagent_type="ork:claude-design-orchestrator", and :4 declares "Requires: claude-design-orchestrator agent". Deleting the agent breaks the skill.
- src/skills/json-render-catalog/SKILL.md:12 has frontmatter `agent: genui-architect`.
- src/skills/implement/SKILL.md:277 names event-driven-architect as a conditional stage-4 spawn.
- security-layer-auditor is referenced by implement/references/agent-teams-security-audit.md, auto/references/routing-rules.md, configure/SKILL.md.
58 skills declare an `agent:` frontmatter binding repo-wide. The auditor's own action ("delete the 12 files, update manifests") would leave dangling subagent_type= references in ~12 skill files with no proposed fix.

Worse, the repo's own classification rule pre-refutes this reasoning and uses one of the auditor's targets as the worked counter-example. src/skills/audit-activation/rules/activation-status.md defines DEAD as "dormant AND no references in ANY skill or agent" and NICHE as "dormant, legitimately specialized + rarely-needed domain (design, multimodal, perf, IaC, security-LLM) and wired into at least one relevant skill -> keep, low use is expected". Its explicit worked example: "**Incorrect** - 'ai-safety-auditor never fired and its description is terse -> prune.' **Correct** - 'ai-safety-auditor never fired BUT is wired into the security-audit team and LLM-safety is a rare task -> NICHE, keep.'" The prior audit's verdict on this exact question was 0 DEAD / 10 NICHE / 7 MIS-TRIGGERED. The rule also warns "'Never fired' = absent from the available telemetry window, which may have gaps" - the auditor never engaged the known Apr-Jun hook outage.

One sub-claim is correct: security-layer-auditor.md:21-24 does declare skills:[security-patterns] and its :86+ 8-Layer Framework is already in src/skills/security-patterns/SKILL.md:116 ("defense-layers.md | 8-layer security architecture (edge to observability)"). Consolidating security-layer-auditor into security-auditor is defensible - and is already the standing recommendation in project memory. The other 11 are not.

refuted.title: The Grounding Protocol is self-refuting on 6 agents (target includes code-quality-reviewer and backend-system-architect)
refuted.reason:
Confirmed on 4 of the 6 named targets, refuted on 2, and the target set is incomplete.

REFUTED - code-quality-reviewer.md: its Grounding Protocol (:68-75) contains NEITHER the string "Delta-0 on Opus" NOR "cheaper tier". It reads "...(subtle-recall 2/4 -> 4/4), while a wrong-domain control stayed flat" with no model-tier claim at all. The self-refutation charge does not apply to it, and the block carries two INFORMATIVE repo-specific pointers - "read the lockfile/manifest" and "cross-check every finding against .claude/rules/antipatterns.md" (that file EXISTS at .claude/rules/antipatterns.md and is loaded as a project instruction).

REFUTED - backend-system-architect.md:74 does not say Delta-0. Verbatim: "...on Opus-tier models the gain narrows to currency/precision". That is a calibrated, non-self-refuting claim - materially different from what the finding quotes it as supporting.

MISSED - infrastructure-architect.md is a 7th `model: inherit` agent carrying a Grounding Protocol (:64). It is absent from the target list, so the arithmetic ("14 carry it; 6 are inherit; keep it on the 8 pinned") is wrong: it is 14 / 7 inherit / 7 pinned.

DELETE-OUTRIGHT IS TOO BLUNT: every one of the 14 blocks ends with "cross-check against .claude/rules/antipatterns.md" plus a read-the-lockfile instruction. Both are non-derivable repo facts. Deleting the block deletes them.

bytes_saved:9,000 is honest: I measured all 14 blocks at 23,609 bytes total (avg 1,686 B), so 6 blocks ~= 10,100 bytes. Not fabricated.

Context the auditor missed: this exact calibration was already made deliberately. Project memory records the 2026-06-24 Opus 4.8 stress test ("grounding's RECALL benefit -> Delta-0 on STRONG models... it holds on WEAK/cheap models... CALIBRATED: ground where it pays, NOT universally") and PR #2641 shipped 14/37 grounded on purpose, explicitly NOT grounding Opus-tier agents. The prose bug is real (calling `inherit` "a cheaper tier" is false under an Opus session) but it is a one-line correction, not a section deletion.

refuted.title: 11 of 36 agents carry a tool allowlist identical to another agent's; only 25 distinct allowlists exist
refuted.reason:
Measured: 29 distinct allowlists across 36 agents, not 25, and only ONE of the four named groups is right.
- CORRECT: {accessibility-specialist, database-engineer, llm-integrator, test-generator} do share a signature.
- WRONG: "3 share another (ai-safety-auditor, debug-investigator, security-auditor)" - only debug-investigator and security-auditor are byte-identical. ai-safety-auditor's list is set-equal but ORDER-different (Read,Bash,Grep... vs Bash,Read,Grep...), so "byte-identical" is false throughout this finding.
- WRONG: "3 more (deployment-manager, frontend-performance-engineer, git-operations-engineer)" - only deployment-manager + git-operations-engineer group; frontend-performance-engineer differs in order.
- WRONG: "3 more (expect-agent, security-layer-auditor, system-design-reviewer)" - system-design-reviewer carries disallowedTools:[Write,Edit,MultiEdit] and expect-agent carries none. By the finding's OWN merge test ("unless its hooks: or disallowedTools differ") these are not merge candidates.
The same defect invalidates Group A of the MERGE finding: ai-safety-auditor's hooks are PreToolUse restrict-bash + security-command-audit with mcpServers:[tavily], while security-auditor is PostToolUse security-command-audit with mcpServers:[] - different enforcement posture, so the finding's own rule disqualifies the merge it proposes.
The KEEP verdict and the enforcement counts are otherwise solid and I confirmed them: 33/36 hooks, 8/36 disallowedTools (exact file list matches), 29/36 non-empty mcpServers, security-auditor.md:30-33, git-operations-engineer.md:34-43 (four PreToolUse guards incl. conflict-predictor + pre-commit-simulation), code-quality-reviewer.md:36-40 agent/block-writes, web-research-analyst.md:38 required_mcp_servers:[tavily].

refuted.title: BEFORE/AFTER: frontend-ui-developer 592 lines -> 46 lines, 'keep the frontmatter wiring verbatim', losing nothing Opus 5 needs
refuted.reason:
The line/byte facts are exact (592 lines, 22,048 bytes - I confirmed both), and most cites land (:104-109 Agent Teams, :111-118 Task Management, :120-126 MCP Tools + Opus 4.8, :129-214 browser CLI manual self-declared duplicate at :130, :217-224 Concrete Objectives, :226-266 Output Format JSON, :482-495 Boundaries/Coordination/Execution). The Agent Teams teammate-name bug is a genuine find. But the proposed AFTER file fails CI on three counts and violates its own stated rule.

(1) It DROPS taskTypes, keywords (10 routing keywords: react, typescript, component, ui, frontend, zod, tanstack, suspense, form, dashboard) and examplePrompts - all present in the real file at :55-70 - while the finding says "keep the frontmatter wiring verbatim". tests/agents/test-agent-frontmatter.sh:3 requires all three on every agent, and :79-82 enforces non-empty taskTypes, >=1 keyword, and exactly 2 examplePrompts. The AFTER block fails `npm run test:agents`, which the action itself tells you to run.
(2) It DROPS `effort: medium` (real file :7), also silently.
(3) Its AFTER description is 288 bytes, over the 250-byte AGENT_DESC_SINGLE_MAX_BYTES hard cap at tests/performance/test-token-overhead.sh:80.
It also deletes the Context Protocol (live, hook-written, CI-tested - see the paths finding above).
The three surviving facts it identifies (@theme tokens, @/lib/animations presets, the /ork:expect auto-nudge with the .claude/state/expect-skip.<sessionId> opt-out) are correctly identified as the non-derivable keepers - :131 confirms the expect nudge verbatim.

missed: tests/performance/test-token-overhead.sh:79-80 is the binding constraint on this entire dimension and is never mentioned. AGENT_DESC_SINGLE_MAX_BYTES=250, AGENT_DESC_TOTAL_MAX_BYTES=6000. Measured at HEAD: 5,314/6,000 used (686 bytes headroom) and max single 249/250. It runs in package.json:21 validate:pre-push. Any description proposal is dead on arrival unless it is byte-neutral or shrinking.

The always-loaded vs on-spawn distinction is never drawn, and it inverts the report's own priority ranking. Agent DESCRIPTIONS (5,314 bytes, ~1,330 tokens) are the recurring per-session tax; agent BODIES (429,828 bytes) load only when spawned. So the 160KB body cut saves ZERO baseline tokens, while the description rewrite - ranked #1 - is the only change that touches the baseline, and it moves it the wrong way. Project memory already states this exact insight: 'a specialist's grounding belongs in its agent-file BODY (loaded only on spawn) NOT its description (baseline-capped, Delta-0) - so grounding is byte-free in baseline.'

src/skills/audit-activation/ - an entire shipped ork skill (SKILL.md, rules/activation-status.md, references/output-format.md, scripts/run-activation-audit.sh, test-cases.json) devoted to this exact question, with a checked-in A/B harness at docs/feat--activation-audit/agent-routing-experiment.mjs. It is the 5th most-used skill in telemetry (21 invocations). The report's #1 finding is the one thing that skill forbids in four separate places, and the report never cites it.

tests/orphans/test-orphan-agents.sh - an existing orphan-agent gate. It passes clean on all 36 agents. 'Never spawned in telemetry' was equated with 'dead' without running the repo's own reachability check, and without accounting for the known Apr-Jun hook outage or the zero-subagent-channel caveat.

58 skills carry an `agent:` frontmatter binding and skill bodies carry subagent_type= dispatches. The CUT and MERGE verdicts would leave dangling references in ~12 skill files; no reference-repair step is proposed for any of them.

## Output Format is the largest single section in the dimension (1,073 lines across 33 files, avg 32 lines each) and every instance is distinct. It is the strongest genuine reduction candidate - an invented per-agent JSON schema that nothing machine-parses (I found no hook or skill that consumes it; src/hooks/src/subagent-stop/output-validator.ts does not read it). The report buried it inside a false 'copy-pasted boilerplate' bucket and so never argued the case on its merits.
infrastructure-architect.md:64 is a 7th `model: inherit` agent carrying a Grounding Protocol, omitted from the Grounding target list.

manifests/ork.json has only 3 entries under `agents` (glob-shaped, not a per-agent list). The repeated action 'update manifests/ork.json' is likely a no-op; the real count gate is bin/validate-counts.sh plus .claude/rules/count-sync.md, and no finding states what the CLAUDE.md/README count deltas would be.

No finding measures what a specialist spawn actually COSTS versus Explore, which is the load-bearing premise of the headline ('exactly the cost that makes a specialist look worse than Explore'). agent-usage.jsonl carries the spawn records; nobody compared per-spawn token cost between the two. The prior audit reached the opposite conclusion from real data: 'Real misroute rate is only ~5% (~57/1040) - this is a distribution problem (catalog not in the default spawn path), not a quality problem', with the dominant lever being the 394 untyped workflow-subagent spawns that default to the generic worker and that no amount of agent-file editing can reach.
verdicts.notes:
Verdict: 3 of 9 findings survive intact, 6 are refuted in whole or in the part that carries the verdict. The report's cite hygiene is good (I spot-checked ~30 file:line references and nearly all resolve within +/-2 lines, and the quoted strings are verbatim), and its byte arithmetic is measured rather than invented. What it lacks is repo awareness: it never opened the four CI gates and the one ork skill that already govern this exact dimension, so its two highest-ranked actions (rewrite all 36 descriptions; delete Context Protocol from 25 agents) would each break a green test and delete live wiring.

Ranked by damage if applied as written:
1. Delete Context Protocol from 25 agents -> destroys pointers to a live, hook-written, schema-locked, CI-tested state file that is populated right now.
2. Rewrite all 36 descriptions -> +5,000 bytes on the ONLY always-loaded surface, hard-fails validate:pre-push on both the single-description and aggregate caps, to buy a routing gain the repo already A/B-tested at Delta-0.
3. Delete 12 agents -> dangling subagent_type= in ~12 skills, breaks /ork:design-import outright (SKILL.md:4 declares the agent a hard requirement, :139 dispatches it).
4. Delete 'boilerplate' -> ~85% of the targeted lines are per-agent unique content, not copy-paste.

What I would actually keep from this report: finding #7 (the model-pinning policy really is a tool-count proxy - git-operations-engineer.md:5-7 runs irreversible history surgery on haiku with effort:low while event-driven-architect holds an opus pin and has never fired), finding #9 (20 files carry rotting version stamps, nothing tests them), the Agent Teams teammate-name bug (three names that resolve to nothing), the two genuinely-templated sections (Task Management 31/34 identical, Status Protocol 34/36 identical - collapse into src/agents/shared/status-protocol.md, which does exist), the self-declared-duplicate browser CLI manual, and the Grounding Protocol prose fix (correct 'cheaper tier (inherit)' rather than delete the block, on the 4 files that actually say it).

Applying the user's own lens to the report itself: the report is strongest exactly where it is boring (frontmatter enforcement is the keeper, KEEP verdict, bytes_saved 0) and weakest where it is confident. Its central rhetorical move - 'the descriptions are precise and barely overlap; the defect is a missing selection signal' - is a well-argued hypothesis that this repo already ran the experiment on and falsified. That is the failure mode the global debugging rule names: premature root-cause commitment without the confirming evidence.

headline: The premise is wrong by 4.4x: the real per-session tax is 23,764 chars (~5.9k tokens), not 121,718 bytes (~30k) — but 74% of it (17,664 chars / 46 skills) buys skills that have never been invoked once in 485 telemetry events, while the five most-used ork skills pay zero index bytes because the repo already solved this and then stopped applying the fix.

upheld: Finding 1 — the 121,718-byte premise is wrong; only name+description of non-flagged skills load. CONFIRMED EXACTLY: 114 SKILL.md exist; `grep -L 'disable-model-invocation: true'` returns exactly 59 names, and those 59 names are a zero-symmetric-difference match against the ork: entries in this session's own skill listing (brainstorm, implement, commit, create-pr, audit-activation, ci-debug all absent as predicted). I independently reproduced the auditor's `sum(len(description))` = 40,315 chars to the character. Index descriptions = 22,582 chars; +59 line prefixes ~= the 23,764 they claim.

Finding 4's measurement — 109 of 114 descriptions contain a 'Use when' clause totalling 14,931 chars. Reproduced EXACTLY with an independent extractor. The prose examples at src/skills/explore/SKILL.md:5 and src/skills/assess/SKILL.md:5 are verbatim correct.

Finding 7 — src/skills/testing-patterns/SKILL.md:4 is a verbatim-correct quote of a pure redirect stub ('Redirect — testing-patterns was split into 5 focused sub-skills…'), and all 5 targets (testing-unit/e2e/integration/llm/perf) are independently present in the same 59-skill index. The stub is a genuine null option.
Finding 8 (audit-full half) — src/skills/audit-full/SKILL.md:5 does read 'leveraging Opus 4.8 1M context' while this session runs Opus 5. Real, always-loaded, stale self-fact.
Finding 9's survivor arithmetic — after removing the 25 named skills, exactly 34 remain, NOT ONE is under 200 chars, and the smallest is github-operations at 201. Reproduced exactly.
Finding 3's factual base — src/skills/brainstorm/SKILL.md carries `disable-model-invocation: true  # M127 A/S5: slash-only` verbatim, and 55 skills carry the flag. The precedent exists.

refuted.title: "Zero content deleted, zero capability lost" — the demotion makes 15 of the 25 skills COMPLETELY UNREACHABLE
refuted.reason: This is the report's load-bearing safety claim and it is false. The auditor asserts "plugins/ork/commands/*.md already exists for each". It does not: plugins/ork/commands/ contains 35 files total, and 14 of the 25 cut candidates have NO command file (storybook-mcp-integration, mcp-visual-output, multi-surface-render, json-render-catalog, testing-patterns, demo-producer, bare-eval, emulate-seed, market-sizing, competitive-analysis, business-case, okr-design, product-analytics, user-research, prioritization). Root cause: 15 of the 25 carry `user-invocable: false` in frontmatter, so no slash command is generated. For those, `disable-model-invocation: true` + `user-invocable: false` = no slash path AND no model path = the skill is dead code. The repo says this in its own words at src/skills/audit-activation/rules/activation-status.md:25: a skill that is `user-invocable: false` + `disable-model-invocation: true` is "a doc skill [that] can't dispatch". PR1 as written silently deletes 15 skills.

refuted.title: "auto 58" is a cross-plugin misattribution — ork:auto has 5 invocations, not 58
refuted.reason: Counted directly from ~/.claude/analytics/skill-usage.jsonl: `ork:auto` = 5, `hq-ext:auto` = 53. The auditor summed a DIFFERENT plugin's router into ork's. This is not cosmetic: finding 3's "decisive number" argument is built on it. With ork:auto at 5, the ork frequency ranking is assess 64 (INDEX), brainstorm 55 (slash), brainstorming 36 (phantom), visualize-plan 34 (INDEX), audit-activation 21 (slash), verify 10 (INDEX). The claim "the five highest-frequency ork skills after assess and auto are ALL slash-only" is flatly false — the #2 and #4 ork skills by volume are index skills. The conclusion "index presence correlates with nothing" is unsupported by its own data.

refuted.title: Finding 2 labels help and release-sync "never invoked" while its own evidence block lists them as invoked
refuted.reason: Finding 2's title is "46 of the 59 index-paying skills have never been invoked" and its target list includes `help` and `release-sync`. Its own evidence sentence two lines earlier reads "help 2, release-sync 1". Confirmed in telemetry: ork:help = 2, ork:release-sync = 1. Two of the 25 proposed cuts are contradicted inside the same finding.

refuted.title: bytes_saved 16,272 for the 25 demotions is inflated 52% — the real figure is 10,672
refuted.reason: I summed the actual description bytes + line overhead for the exact 25 named skills: 10,672 chars. The 16,272 figure is the total for a DIFFERENT set (the 46 never-invoked, which I measure at 18,756) and is then re-used verbatim in finding 9 for the whole demote+cap program. The same number is claimed twice for two different scopes.

refuted.title: Finding 4's 11,000 bytes saved is impossible — only 8,154 chars of 'Use when' sit inside the index
refuted.reason: Of the 14,931 'Use when' chars, only 8,154 belong to the 59 index skills. The other 6,777 sit on slash-only skills that, per the report's own finding 1, cost zero at runtime. Deleting EVERY index tail caps the saving at 8,154, and the report says only the restatement tails go. Worse, the claimed savings sum to 16,272 + 11,000 + 244 + 90 = 27,606 chars against a 23,764-char index — the report proposes saving more bytes than exist.

refuted.reason: Scanning descriptions for negative/redirect markers returns 16: auto, ci-debug, cover, design-import, design-ship, design-stylecards, dev, dream, implement, mcp-visual-output, portless, quickviz, swarm-migrate, testing-patterns, verify, zustand-patterns. refuted.title: Demoting design-import AND design-ship destroys the exact disambiguator finding 5 says is the only thing resolving their collision
refuted.reason: Finding 5 identifies design-import<>design-ship as the #2 measured collision (0.232) and prescribes keeping the one-line boundary. Both descriptions already carry it verbatim (design-import: "…when that same scaffold should carry on through test generation, browser verification and an opened PR, run /ork:design-ship instead"; design-ship: "…if all you need is the components written to disk, run /ork:design-import instead"). Finding 2 removes BOTH from the index. The prescription and the action cancel.

refuted.title: design-context-extract is on the CUT list and is the one skill the report itself certifies as earning its bytes
refuted.reason: Finding 4 holds up src/skills/design-context-extract/SKILL.md:5 — "Use when the user provides, uploads, links, or points to a screenshot, URL, or video" — as the model of a keeper because it "encodes an INPUT SHAPE, not a synonym — that is real routing signal." Finding 2 then demotes it. That skill's entire activation model is the model noticing a pasted screenshot; a user who pastes an image does not then type /ork:design-context-extract. verdicts.notes:
Verdict: the auditor's METROLOGY is real and reproducible; its REMEDIATION is unsafe.

The single most valuable claim in the report is correct and I confirmed it independently to the character: the always-loaded index is 59 lines / ~23.8k chars, not 121,718 bytes. `grep -L 'disable-model-invocation: true'` over src/skills/*/SKILL.md returns exactly the 59 names present in this session's own ork: listing, zero symmetric difference. Their description-sum (40,315) matched my extractor exactly, as did the 'Use when' count (109 / 14,931) and the survivor floor (34 skills, min 201 at github-operations). These were measured, not fabricated.

Everything downstream of the measurement degrades. The cut list was assembled from a telemetry partition containing a cross-plugin misattribution (hq-ext:auto counted as ork:auto, 53 events), a phantom skill (ork:brainstorming, 36 events, no directory), and two skills labelled never-invoked that the same paragraph reports as invoked. It was then sized with a byte figure belonging to a different set (16,272 for a set costing 10,672), and justified by a safety claim I falsified in one command: 14 of the 25 targets have no generated slash command because 15 carry `user-invocable: false`. On those, the proposed edit is not a demotion, it is a deletion.

SALVAGE — what actually survives and is worth shipping:
1. Re-baseline to 23,764 chars / ~5.9k tokens. Unconditional keeper. Kills every future proposal to trim tags/license/compatibility for token savings.
2. Demote ONLY index skills that (a) have `user-invocable: true`, so a slash command exists, AND (b) are not referenced in any agent's `skills:` list. On the current list that is roughly design-import, design-ship, design-to-code, design-stylecards, telemetry-inspect, prd-to-goal, help, dev — minus any that fail the agent-reference check. Real saving on the order of 4-5k chars, not 16k. Explicitly EXCLUDE design-context-extract (screenshot-upload trigger) and the whole `user-invocable: false` reference tier.
3. audit-full's 'Opus 4.8' -> fix all 4 occurrences, not just :5.
4. testing-patterns redirect stub -> it is `user-invocable: false` with no command file, so do NOT flag it. Delete the skill outright or fold the redirect into the five sub-skills. Flagging it is the 15-skill bug in miniature.
5. The 200-char cap: do not land it. Land the boundary-clause additions from finding 6 (errors vs fix-issue, create-pr vs review-pr, explore vs visualize-plan) instead — those are cheap, additive, and INFORMATIVE, and they do not require 33 unwritten rewrites or a fight with auto's routing table.

Against the operating thesis: this dimension does NOT support it. The index tax is 5.9k tokens, not 30k, and the defensible cut is ~1k tokens, not 4k. The genuinely hobbling text here is the 'Use when' synonym tail (8,154 index chars, real), which is a prose problem, not a scaffolding problem.

SCORE: 7 upheld / 4 refuted, but two of the upheld ones carry a broken remedy.

WHAT SURVIVES CLEANLY
- Finding 11 (emphasis density KEEP) is the only finding whose numbers I reproduced exactly, and its "do NOT sweep, you will corrupt security severity rubrics" call is correct and the highest-value line in the report.
- Finding 10 (eval-runner.md:69 as house-style exemplar) is verified verbatim and is genuinely the right template: names the file, the fields, a concrete retired ID, and the reason.
- Findings 9 and 10 reporting NEGATIVE results instead of manufacturing hits is the right behaviour and should be credited.

WHAT THE PATTERN OF ERRORS IS
Every refutation traces to the same failure: the auditor asserted a MECHANISM without opening the file that implements it.
- Asserted `compatibility:` is always-loaded -> tests/performance/test-token-overhead.sh says descriptions of user-invocable skills only.
- Asserted models.vocab.json holds xhigh capability -> zero occurrences of "xhigh" in that file.
- Asserted `claude-sonnet-4-6` would 404 -> it is in fullIds and the vocab lint PASSES.
- Asserted collapsing to Read() saves tokens -> the shared file is 10x the inline enum and is loaded per spawn.

BLAST RADIUS IF APPLIED AS WRITTEN
Finding 4 (delete 83 compatibility lines) breaks a stamp target added by PR #3141 one day before the audit and removes the per-skill anchor the next CC floor bump needs.
Finding 6 (cut 12 of 14 NEVERs) deletes the `@/lib/dates` / `useFormatting` / `@/lib/animations` / i18n-key wiring, which is the exact class of non-derivable fact the brief defines as a KEEPER.
Finding 7 edits working code on a false 404 premise.
Finding 5 increases per-spawn token cost across 1,135 specialist spawns.

1. Extend tests/skills/structure/test-model-recency.sh to catch prose model-tier claims (root cause of finding 3; without it the sweep re-rots at Opus 6).
2. Rewrite doctor Category 14 as a capability statement, and fix src/skills/assess/SKILL.md:54,56 in the SAME change. Do NOT route it through models.vocab.json until that file gains an effort field.
3. Delete the 10 `## Opus 4.8: 128K Output Tokens` sections (2,368 bytes, genuinely stale + generic).
4. Delete the 32 TaskCreate tutorials (11,324 bytes).
5. Delete the 20 memory-boilerplate lines - all 20 files already carry `memory:` frontmatter or mcp__memory__ tools, so nothing is lost.
6. On frontend-ui-developer: do NOT cut the 12. Cut the ~3 truly generic ones, and separately decide whether a plugin-shipped agent should carry a foreign project's module paths at all - that is the real bug in that file.
Leave findings 4, 5, and 7 alone.

A CRUD app with DDD is a red flag.' That is exactly the calibrated judgement content the auditor says is missing, and the proposed delete destroys it.

refuted.title: 'The 97-never-invoked telemetry number is fully explained: 39 of them CANNOT be invoked'
refuted.reason: This synthesis collapses with the reachability error. At most 9 skills are structurally unreachable, so the never-invoked count is overwhelmingly NOT explained by unreachability. The auditor also never engaged the two telemetry caveats the brief explicitly flagged: the April-June hook outage and the possibly-broken subagent channel (90/90 events channel=main, zero subagent). Agent-declared skills load inside subagent runs -- precisely the channel with zero capture -- so the telemetry is blind to the exact usage path that would exonerate the 30 wired skills.

missed: The hidden set is 45 skills, not 39. The auditor silently dropped six that meet its own dmi=true + ui=false criterion: architecture-decision-record, browser-tools, chain-patterns, code-review-playbook, configure, scope-appropriate-architecture. No selection rule is stated, so the sample looks curated to fit the conclusion.

`configure` is a genuine orphan the audit never mentions: dmi=true, ui=false, zero agent refs, zero skill refs. It is a better CUT candidate than most of the 39 and does not appear anywhere in the report.

The real orphan list, which the audit should have produced, is 9: skill-evolution, notebooklm, upgrade-assessment, feedback, presentation-builder, checkpoint-resume, validate-counts, release-checklist, audit-skills (plus configure = 10). Even here the audit would have had to do more work: skill-evolution is named in ork:auto's routing description, and 'feedback' appears in 39 files under src/hooks/src and 2 workflows -- so at least two of the 10 have non-frontmatter wiring that a blind delete would break.

10 skills carry dmi=true AND user-invocable=true. They are hidden from the model index but ARE live slash commands. The auditor's claim that 'all 55 dmi=true skills are absent' from the listing conflates these with the 45 fully-hidden ones and gets the index arithmetic right only by accident.

No deletion was tested. The report never runs `npm run test:skills`, `npm run test:agents`, or `bin/validate-counts.sh` against a single proposed cut, despite CLAUDE.md naming all three as gates and despite tests/agents enforcing the very `skills` field the audit claims is unused. Every 'risk: low' rating is unvalidated.
The brief said 36 agents; there are 37 .md files in src/agents/. The auditor propagated the brief's number without counting, which is how the 36-agent `skills:` blocks went unread.

No analysis of which skills the 6 never-spawned agents pull in. If claude-design-orchestrator, demo-producer, design-context-extractor, event-driven-architect, genui-architect and security-layer-auditor are dead, the skills reachable ONLY through them are transitively dead -- that is the actual defensible cut path the reachability graph enables, and the audit missed it entirely by asserting the graph was empty.

The 'REWRITE the six indexed pattern-libraries, ~90% reduction, 1,350,000 bytes' finding names no measurement method. Unlike every other byte figure (which reproduced exactly), this one is a round number applied to a hand-waved 90% and is the only savings claim in the report I could not reproduce.
verdicts.notes:
Method: rebuilt the skill reachability graph from scratch by parsing every `skills:` YAML block in src/agents/*.md and src/skills/*/SKILL.md, then re-measured every byte figure with find|wc -c and every quote with sed against the cited line ranges.

Split verdict. The auditor's measurement work is honest -- the 39-skill byte total reproduces to the byte (3,597,567), per-skill figures matched exactly, and every quoted line I checked exists verbatim at roughly the cited line. The product-frameworks duplication, the testing-patterns redirect stub, the brainstorming telemetry refutation, and the index-size premise correction all survive and are worth acting on.

But the report's spine is a single fabricated grep result. "`grep -h '^skills:' src/agents/*.md` returns EMPTY" is false -- 36 of 37 agents declare skills, the field survives into plugins/, and tests/agents/test-frontend-performance-engineer.sh:41 requires it. That one false negative cascades into 8 CUT/MERGE findings covering ~700 KB of proposed deletions plus a CLAUDE.md edit that would replace a true statement with a false one and add a validate-counts gate that fails on 30 correctly-wired skills.

The pattern is diagnostic: a claim of absence was asserted rather than executed, and every downstream "risk: low" inherits it. Corrected numbers: 45 hidden skills (not 39), 30 of the audited 39 statically wired, 9-10 true orphans, and the defensible cut is roughly one fifth of the headline. Recommend rejecting the reachability-based findings wholesale and re-running the audit off the actual graph; the transitive-deadness path through the 6 never-spawned agents is the analysis that should have been done.
